findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded for web requests, so fallbacks silently fail in background jobs and mailers
findings.body: The translate accelerator loads locale files lazily: only locales passed through `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`load_locale` are ever read from disk into the backend. The new `FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from `ApplicationController#set_locale`, i.e. during HTTP requests. Any translation done outside a request cycle (Sidekiq jobs, scheduled email digests, `UserNotifications` mailers, etc.) will only have the current locale loaded; the fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]` will be consulted by the backend but those locale files were never loaded, so lookups fall through to 'translation missing' instead of English. The fallback loading should happen wherever `I18n.locale` is set (or on first translation), not only in the controller before_filter.

findings.title: Mixed string/symbol locales defeat uniq and loaded-locale tracking
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`. `locale` here is whatever was passed in (frequently a String such as "en" when it comes from user input or `I18n.locale` assigned from a string), while the other entries are symbols. `"en"` and `:en` are not `uniq`-equal, so the list can contain duplicates, and more importantly `ensure_loaded!` passes the string into `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, which checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` in the accelerator. Since other code paths push symbols (e.g. `config.locale`) into `@loaded_locales`, a string locale will never match and `load_locale` will be taken (acquiring the global LOAD_MUTEX) on every request for that user. Normalizing `locale.to_sym` in `[]` would avoid the repeated mutex lock and duplicate work.

findings.title: Translation LRU cache is keyed only on current locale, so fallback results go stale when the site default locale changes
findings.body: With fallbacks now active, the result of `translate_no_cache(key)` depends not just on `config.locale` but on the whole fallback chain, which includes `SiteSetting.default_locale`. The cache key `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"` does not include the fallback list, so if an admin changes the site's default locale, entries previously cached (translated via the old default locale fallback) will keep being served for users of other locales until they happen to be evicted from the 300-entry LRU or the process restarts. Including `SiteSetting.default_locale` (or the resolved fallback chain) in the cache key would make the cache correct.
